test: Part 1: for won NEW quotes, match quote lines to later order jobs by customer+part (first job after quote), and compare quote-stage estimated hours by work centre (setup + run_per_piece x job quantity) with actual clocked labour hours on that job's operation at the same work centre; report median and pooled actual/estimate by work centre, by year, with counts. Also compare quote hours to the job routing estimate to see whether the routing or the quote carries the padding. Check work_date truncation is irrelevant (hours summed per op, not per day). Part 2: among decided NEW quotes (won/lost/expired/no award), compute est_hours per $ of est_material (and labour share of quoted price) and test hit rate across quintiles, within customer segment and year, and within customer (customer-demeaned).
support: Quote-stage actual/estimate pooled below ~0.9 at laser, brake, mill, lathe, paint, assembly but ~1 at weld; AND hit rate declining monotonically across hours-per-material-dollar quintiles, persisting within year/segment/customer.
weaken: Quote-stage hours match actuals (ratio ~1) even though routings don't; or hit rate flat across labour intensity quintiles or the gradient disappears within customer/year; or ratio depends on matching artefacts.
expect: Moderate confidence that quote-stage ratios are below 1 outside weld (routing likely derived from quote). Low confidence that hit rate varies meaningfully with labour intensity; I expect a weak or confounded relation, e.g. driven by part size/quantity or customer mix, so the overpricing->hit-rate link probably won't hold strongly.
